are_you_ok.title: Heavy rain drenches Colorado
are_you_ok.summary: A wet stretch moved across Colorado: forecasters warned first of flash flooding on Friday and Saturday, especially over burn scars — hillsides stripped by past wildfires where rain runs off instead of soaking in. Severe thunderstorms then hit Denver and the plains east of the mountains with rain and hail on Saturday afternoon, and by the end of the weekend the rain had left roads and trails muddy and put parts of the Denver metro, southeast of Boulder, under flood warnings.
are_you_ok.description: Heavy rain soaked parts of Colorado this weekend, leaving roads and trails muddy and prompting flood warnings in portions of the Denver metro area.

are_you_ok.title: 'Nothing left here': Westminster lake shrinks as Colorado drought has forced 48 closures
are_you_ok.summary: Drought pushed McKay Lake in Westminster, a suburb between Boulder and Denver, low enough that Colorado Parks and Wildlife ordered an emergency fish salvage — lifting all catch limits so anglers with a license could take fish that would otherwise die. The lake is one of 48 waters the state has had to close or restrict as the drought deepens.
are_you_ok.description: Colorado Parks and Wildlife issued an emergency fish salvage at McKay Lake due to severe drought, lifting all bag and possession limits.

conversation_starters.summary: Boulder's plan to make the downtown Pearl Street shopping district all-electric is getting smaller. Xcel, the utility that supplies gas and electricity to Boulder and most of Colorado, now says only about 24 buildings are connected to the aging downtown gas line, well down from the 66 originally believed — and those customers will be able to keep their natural gas service.

you_should_know.title: Colorado minimum wage will jump in 2027 to $15.71/hour, $12.69 tipped
you_should_know.summary: Colorado set its 2027 minimum wage at $15.71 an hour, $12.69 for tipped workers — a 3.6% bump from the current rate and about 41% above what the state's floor was in 2019.
you_should_know.description: According to the DLSS, the new wage of $15.71 represents a 3.6% increase over the current wage and a 41.5% increase from the wage in 2019 of $11.10 an hour.
